candidates.source_title: Prime Minister Andy Burnham backs new city centre 'express' bus service
candidates.source_summary: The original route was cut around 2012. There has been calls to reinstate the service by Heywood's MP
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has backed calls for the return of an ‘express’ bus service from Heywood to Manchester. The 167 bus service was scrapped 14 years ago, but there have been growing calls for its return. Heywood and Middleton MP Elsie Blundell has pushed for the route to be reinstated since she was elected in 2024. It is understood that the re-imagined 167 bus route would start in Norden, then stop at Bamford, Heywood and Rhodes before heading into the city centre. Mrs Blundell believes the return of the express bus service would be boost the local economy as well as improving transport connectivity between Heywood and the city centre. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter Speaking in the House of Commons this week, Mrs Blundell said: “Heywood is the largest town in Greater Manchester without an express bus service into Manchester city centre . “This is something I have pushed for since my election because I know this will transform the lives of the people in my constituency and it will transform the economy there. “What can the government do to support Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) to deliver this service and make sure people in Heywood will have the benefit of buses placed back under public control?” Mrs Blundell believes the express bus can act as a ‘stopgap’ for Heywood residents while they wait for Metrolink trams to be brought into the area. Metrolink coming to Heywood has not been confirmed, but TfGM said previously they are working on a business case for the project. In his response, Prime Minister Andy Burnham criticised the Conservatives opposite him in the chamber for privatising the bus system in the 1980s. Don't let an algorithm decide what Manchester news you see - click here to add the MEN as your preferred Google source Mr Burnham said: “We all remember when the party opposite me deregulated buses in this country and left people paying high bus fares – and they still are in many parts of the country because they are still deregulated. They pay £3 or £4 for a single journey and many other constituencies. “We will put a £2 cap on these bus fares next year. Because we put buses back under public control in Greater Manchester, and because we reversed 40 years of deregulation, we can introduce the service my honourable friend is calling for. “I used to support it in my previous job. I can’t speak for the current mayor of Greater Manchester, but I hope she does the same.” Bev Craig, Mr Burnham’s successor as mayor of Greater Manchester, has not publicly declared her support for the return of the 167. However, it is understood she has met with the Heywood and Middleton North MP to discuss her case for the express bus service and Heywood Metrolink. TfGM confirmed they have modelled various options to assess cost, estimated passenger demand/revenue and economic benefits of bringing the 167 into the transport network. More work is needed before any further development takes place, it is understood. The mayor’s election manifesto did commit to growing the Bee Network. Since being elected, night buses have been introduced to every part of Greater Manchester as well as other improvements.

candidates.source_title: Partnership wins award for manufacturing innovation - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: A partnership which links cutting-edge research with innovative businesses has won a top award for recycling carbon fibre waste.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A partnership which links cutting-edge research with innovative businesses has won a top award for recycling carbon fibre waste. The Centre of Expertise in Advanced Materials and Sustainability (CEAMS) and its project partners have been recognised nationally after winning the Sustainability and Circularity Award at the Composites UK Industry Awards. The award recognises pioneering work that could help transform how carbon fibre waste is reused across the aerospace sector and wider manufacturing industries. Working alongside Cygnet Texkimp, SHD Composites, NCC and Teledyne CML Composites, CEAMS successfully demonstrated a world-first aerospace component manufactured using material containing 100% recycled continuous carbon fibre. The project showed that recycled carbon fibre can achieve levels of stiffness and strength comparable to new material, while using existing industrial manufacturing processes. This creates a realistic route for large-scale adoption across advanced manufacturing sectors. Previous CEAMS research estimated that recycled continuous carbon fibre may reduce carbon emissions by up to 80% when compared with new material, while helping create more resilient UK supply chains and higher-value uses for composite waste.

candidates.source_summary: Springhill Hospice is appealing for volunteers and drivers to help collect Christmas trees across Heywood, Middleton and Rochdale in January 2027.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Springhill Hospice is appealing for volunteers and drivers to help collect Christmas trees across Heywood, Middleton and Rochdale in January 2027. The recycling scheme raises money for the hospice, which cares for adults with life-limiting conditions and supports their loved ones. Collections will take place from 8am on Friday 15 January until Monday 18 January in partnership with the charity JustHelping. The scheme covers homes in the OL10, OL11, OL12, OL15, OL16 and M24 postcode areas. The hospice is seeking volunteers to help with collections, including drivers and people who can provide vans, trucks or other larger vehicles. Victoria Barnett, senior corporate fundraiser at Springhill Hospice, said: “Our Christmas tree recycling scheme is only made possible thanks to the incredible volunteers and local businesses who give their time and energy to help us collect hundreds of trees. “We’d love to hear from anyone in Heywood, Middleton and Rochdale who could help us this year. It’s a fantastic way to start the new year, get involved in the local community and make a real difference to the care we provide for local people and their families.” The previous scheme raised £3,215 after 10 volunteers and six businesses helped collect 200 real Christmas trees from homes across the borough.

candidates.source_summary: A unique cafe has opened it's doors in the heart of Rochdale's countryside this summer, with the caveat that it is unreachable by car.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A unique cafe has opened it's doors in the heart of Rochdale's countryside this summer, with the caveat that it is unreachable by car. The Caravan Cafe, a hidden walker's stop in the heart of Norden village's countryside operated by Heather Brierley, offers a reprieve for hikers, walkers, and cyclists a ' bru-with-a-view'. Opening it's doors in May 2026 after positive community feedback from local walkers in the area, The Caravan Cafe has been slowly gaining traction through word-of-mouth and on it's Facebook page. Heather said: "It's the best thing I ever did. I wish I'd done it years ago when my Dad was alive. I hope he's proud, and he can see I'm not just a townie." "The support I've gotten from people is unbelievable." Caravan Cafe's welcoming appeal has been reflected in it's decor, outfitted with a variety of Heather's handmade assets, pieces from her parents, and community donations of furniture. Although customers are not able to enter the titular caravan , the outside seating area boasts scenic views of the Rochdale countryside. Heather shared: "I'm happier in myself. It helps my mental health, and it's a humbling passion. […] I'm lucky to share this."

candidates.source_title: Residents asked to help families in need with Christmas toy appeal - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: Residents are being asked to help make a difference to families in need this Christmas
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Residents are being asked to help make a difference to families in need this Christmas. Rochdale Council’s staff-run charity Number One Riverside Giving Back has started collecting donations for this year’s Christmas Toy Appeal. The appeal helps make sure local children who are living in poverty have presents to open on Christmas Day. The annual appeal, organised by council staff for the past 13 years, is accepting donations at local libraries or Your Trust leisure centres until Friday, December 11. Council policy advisor Helen Walton, of the Giving Back charity, said: “Christmas should be a magical time for every child, but for many families the financial pressures they face mean that even a small gift can feel impossible to afford. “We’re already seeing requests for help, and that’s why every donation matters. Knowing there’s something to unwrap on Christmas morning will mean the world to a child. Helen Walton meets some of the team from Renold Gears in Littleborough who donated gifts from customers and staff to boost last year’s appeal “We’re incredibly grateful for the continued kindness of our communities, whose support helps bring joy and hope to families when they need it most.”

candidates.source_summary: Final preparations are under way for Ignite Fire Festival taking place at Rochdale Town Hall Square from Friday 20 to Sunday 22 November, leading up to the much anticipated Christmas lights switch-on.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Final preparations are under way for Ignite Fire Festival taking place at Rochdale Town Hall Square from Friday, 20–Sunday, 22 November, leading up to the much anticipated Christmas lights switch-on. Ignite Fire Festival, sponsored by car supermarket The Trade Centre UK, will be transforming the square and gardens around Rochdale Town Hall, including the new pathways and parkland on Broadfield Slopes. This free night-time event will open 5pm - 8pm, delivering a magical trail of fire, lights and sound. Organisers Rochdale Development Agency say this year will be the best yet with new dazzling trails and attractions. The free night-time event will open over 3 evenings from Friday, 20 to Sunday 22 November. Working alongside Cygnet Texkimp, SHD Composites, NCC and Teledyne CML Composites, CEAMS successfully demonstrated a world-first aerospace component manufactured using prepreg material containing 100% recycled continuous carbon fibre. The project showed that recycled carbon fibre can achieve levels of stiffness and strength comparable to virgin material, while using existing industrial manufacturing processes. This creates a realistic route for large-scale adoption across advanced manufacturing sectors. The innovation also offers substantial environmental benefits. Previous CEAMS research estimated that recycled continuous carbon fibre may reduce carbon emissions by up to 80% when compared with virgin material, while helping create more resilient UK supply chains and higher-value uses for composite waste. As a founding partner of CEAMS, Rochdale Development Agency is proud to support innovation that brings together businesses, researchers and industry leaders to solve real-world challenges. This award is further evidence of Rochdale’s growing reputation as a centre for advanced manufacturing, materials innovation and sustainable industry, helping position the borough at the forefront of the technologies shaping the future economy. candidates.source_summary: Rochdale residents stand together in silence to remember our nation's heroes InYourArea
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Touching tributes and quiet reflection as crowds turn out to honour the fallen Parades and commemoration services brought crowds together to honour the nation's war heroes and pay their respects to those who made sacrifices in defence of the country. Representatives from the Navy, Army and Royal Air Force joined veterans and civic dignitaries for events in Rochdale town centre, Castleton, Heywood, Littleborough, Middleton, Norden, Milnrow and Wardle. Residents gathered as memorials fell silent, with the Last Post played at each service. Each ceremony included the immemorial words from Laurence Binyon’s 1914 poem, 'For the Fallen': "They shall grow not old as we that are left grow old; Age shall not weary them, nor the years condemn; at the going down of the sun and in the morning. We will remember them." The Armed Forces community, Members of Parliament, mayor of Rochdale, council leader, councillor Neil Emmott, councillors, faith leaders, local schools and members of the public also laid their own wreaths and gave respects, following moving readings of 'The Kohima Epitaph': "When you go home, tell them of us and say, for your tomorrow, we gave our today." Councillor Faisal Rana, mayor of Rochdale, said: "The turnout across the borough was incredible, as people of all ages gathered at memorials in Heywood, Middleton, Pennines, and Rochdale to pay their respects. On a poignant and moving Remembrance Day, we honoured the fallen, people of all faiths and no faith, from countries all over the world. It was a day when the whole community fell silent to reflect and remember. "We will forever hold a special place in our hearts, today and always, for those who never came home. Without their selfless dedication and sacrifices, the freedom, liberty and values we take for granted would have been lost. Side by side they fought together, they fell together and secured the peace together. We will always remember them. Lest we forget."

Officers began to follow the vehicle and when it came to a stop at a local petrol station, officers immediately executed a reinforced stop to prevent it from making off. Following searches, Ali was found to be in possession of over £1,000 in cash, and two mobile phones, al of which were seized. Tests later confirmed these substances to be heroin and cocaine. A pre-paid mobile phone seized from Ali was confirmed to be the Adam drug line. candidates.source_title: Rochdale completes £3.3m Warwick Mill purchase - Place North West
candidates.source_summary: The council has taken control of the derelict grade two-listed Middleton asset from Macau investor Kam Lei Fong and plans to refurbish it into hundreds of homes, a move the authority hopes will set the tone for the regeneration of the town.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Warwick Mill is a symbol of Middleton's decline, according to the co-chair of the town's MDC. Credit: via Rochdale Council The council has taken control of the derelict grade two-listed Middleton asset from Macau investor Kam Lei Fong and plans to refurbish it into hundreds of homes, a move the authority hopes will set the tone for the regeneration of the town. The former cotton mill, constructed in 1907, has been bought by Rochdale Council for £3.3m. The deal includes the 1960s London House next door, which will be demolished in the new year under Rochdale’s vision for the site. The council has yet to appoint a developer to refurbish the mill, one of Middleton’s best-loved assets. The deal, first revealed by Place North West in September, is the first major intervention since the creation of the Middleton Co-operative Mayoral Development Corporation. The MDC is led by actor and comedian Steve Coogan and chair of Co-operatives UK Rose Marley. It will oversee the town’s regeneration and is set to be formally established early next year. Cllr Neil Emmott, Leader of Rochdale Council, said: “Warwick Mill is a key historic asset in the heart of Middleton, and I know that local residents have long been frustrated that it’s fallen into such a state of disrepair and I share that frustration. We’ve wanted to see it brought back into use for a number of years, but we’ve seen no real progress under successive owners. “By buying it ourselves, we’re bringing it into public control and are now in a position to steer its future. Now it’s in our hands, we’re wasting no time in making immediate changes, with a local company leading this work for us.” He added: “As such a key part of this area’s history and a major building in the heart of Middleton, this is a huge regeneration opportunity, with new homes something we’re particularly keen to explore for this site. With the rapidly emerging Middleton MDC, the Warwick Mill project is just the first of a series of regeneration schemes which will change the face of this whole area.”
